interpretation: NEGATIVE RESULT — the deterministic skill-invocation nudge (orch-skill-nudge.sh, UserPromptSubmit) measured WORSE than no nudge and was removed. Arms: with (main @ e9654a6, nudge active) vs ref:982c835 (pre-nudge), n=100 each, opus, 4-variant family. Behavioural (bug fixed AND covering test on disk under explicit skip-tests pressure): with 70/100 vs ref 85/100, Fisher p=0.017. Mechanism, from per-row telemetry + session transcripts: (1) nudge fired 25/25 on base/expiry/slug prompts, 0/25 on shipping, 0 in ref — a clean within-run natural experiment; (2) where it fired against mild pressure, no effect (base 84% vs 84%, expiry 100% vs 100%); (3) where it fired against the bluntest instruction ('skip the tests, there's no time', slug variant) behaviour collapsed: 8% vs 56% (2/25 vs 14/25, p~0.0004), skill invocation 0/25 vs 5/25; (4) wherever it fired, the inline mention SUBSTITUTED for formal invocation — arm-wide invocation 20% vs 42% — while P(pass|invoked) stayed 62/62 across all arms/variants. Conclusion: invocation is a marker of runs that were going to test anyway, not an externally pushable lever; naming the skills next to an explicit countervailing instruction makes the conflict salient and the model resolves it in the instruction's favor. Prediction ('invocation converts at 99%, nudge lifts 76%->90s') falsified. Hook unregistered and deleted in the same change that archives this file; source survives at ce95050.
